title: Driveline / Transfer Case — Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance (P0879)
shortDescription: AWD/4WD driveline or transmission control fault: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance. Stored as P0879.
fullDescription: Modern AWD and part-time 4WD systems use the TCM and transfer case control module to manage fluid pressure, clutch engagement, shift solenoids, and mode switching between 2H/4H/4L. Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance indicates the controller has detected a circuit, range, or performance fault that may cause the system to lock, default to 2WD, or refuse range changes. Driveline binding and transmission slip can result if ignored.
safetyImpact: Driveable; loss of AWD/4WD engagement, possible transmission limp mode, and reduced traction in poor conditions.

causes.cause: Failed transfer case shift motor or encoder
Low or contaminated transmission/transfer case fluid
Faulty solenoid or pressure sensor
Wiring chafe at transfer case harness
TCM or transfer case module failure

fixSteps.title: Read Module Data
fixSteps.instruction: Pull TCM and transfer case module data; record commanded vs actual range and clutch duty cycle.

fixSteps.title: Check Fluid Level and Condition
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect transfer case and transmission fluid level, color, and smell — burnt fluid implies clutch wear.

fixSteps.title: Test Shift Motor Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe shift motor / solenoid connector and verify supply, ground, and resistance against spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed shift motor, encoder, solenoid pack, or harness as identified; relearn module if required.

faq.q: Can I drive in 2WD until repaired?
faq.a: Usually yes — most systems default to 2WD; avoid towing and slick roads.

faq.q: Is fluid service likely to fix it?
faq.a: If fluid is dark or low, a service plus relearn resolves a meaningful share of these faults before parts replacement.
